situation: A large partner asked to skip the standard maintenance notice to get a fix sooner.
decision: Decline the full upgrade tomorrow, offer a narrower fix for that partner, and explain why.

moves.name: ask who carries the cost of saying yes
moves.step: Look past the requester to everyone else who bears the risk of an exception.
moves.cue: a request for an exception to a protective rule
moves.evidence: who else carries the cost if I say yes

moves.name: check whether the change is reversible
moves.step: Let reversibility decide how much risk an exception can carry.
moves.cue: a change requested on short notice
moves.evidence: If we can roll the database back in minutes, the risk to everyone else is small

moves.name: offer a smaller version of the request
moves.step: Find a narrower action that gives the requester most of what they need.
moves.cue: a request that would spend others' trust
moves.evidence: Can we hotfix just the bug for them

moves.name: explain the why so it travels
moves.step: Give the reason with the answer so an intermediary can carry it.
moves.cue: a decision relayed through an account manager
moves.evidence: I'd say why, so the account manager can take that back to the partner

considerations.evidence: it's there for every other customer who plans around our windows
